- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment swings from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model delays mean reversion — force a 1–2 day lagged correction toward historical mean.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3), model overestimates upward momentum — reduce forecast slope by 10–15%.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model still holds high values — reduce forecast by 3–5% per day until reversion confirmed.
- Model consistently underestimates downward moves when sentiment is mildly negative — add 2–3% buffer to downward forecasts if sentiment < -0.20.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is volatile (±0.3+ in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
